reason: The text describes an Assyrian military delegation (the Rab-Shakeh) attempting to persuade the people of Jerusalem to abandon their trust in King Hezekiah and surrender to Sennacherib. However, the people respond with complete loyalty and silence: 'And the people held their peace and answered him not a word; for the king's commandment was, saying, Do not answer him' (וְהֶחֱרִישׁוּ הָעָם וְלֹא־ עָנוּ אֹתוֹ דָּבָר כִּי־ מִצְוַת הַמֶּלֶךְ). The people obey Hezekiah's command to remain silent and refuse to be swayed by external propaganda. There is no evidence of internal antagonism from the regular people toward their leader; the antagonism comes entirely from the Assyrian invaders.
